stem: During pancreas transplant evaluation, a candidate reports frequent severe hypoglycemic episodes despite optimized management. How should the coordinator classify this finding?

options.text: A frequent or severe metabolic complication supporting end-organ failure assessment
An irrelevant symptom that never affects pancreas candidacy
An automatic contraindication that prohibits any transplant evaluation
Evidence that the candidate no longer has diabetes

explanation.rationale_correct: Pancreas candidate selection includes frequent or severe metabolic complications such as hypo- or hyperglycemia, ketoacidosis, and hypoglycemic unawareness despite optimized medical management.

rationale_incorrect.B: Metabolic complications are objective measures of end-organ failure considered during pancreas evaluation.
rationale_incorrect.C: Severe metabolic complications are assessed for suitability rather than automatically prohibiting evaluation.
rationale_incorrect.D: Hypoglycemic episodes reflect ongoing diabetes-related metabolic instability rather than resolution of diabetes.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 15, Pancreas Transplantation → Candidate Selection Criteria → B.2.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Frequent or severe metabolic complications … Hypo- or hyperglycemia … Hypoglycemic unawareness despite optimized medical management

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 15 → Candidate Selection Criteria → B.2. (frequent/severe metabolic complications including hypoglycemic unawareness); PDF p. 825 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Twelfth 020300 item; pancreas metabolic-complication angle distinct from PAK (cctc-2050) and alcohol contract (cctc-2058); anchor verified on Cupples p. 825.

stem: A candidate is referred for simultaneous heart-lung transplantation. Which evaluation scope aligns with standard references?

options.text: Evaluation includes procedures outlined for both heart and lung transplantation
Only isolated kidney evaluation is required
No cardiac or pulmonary testing is performed before heart-lung transplant
Only dental assessment is required without cardiopulmonary studies

explanation.rationale_correct: The heart-lung transplant evaluation process includes procedures outlined in the sections on heart transplantation and lung transplantation.

rationale_incorrect.B: Heart-lung evaluation requires cardiopulmonary assessment rather than isolated kidney studies alone.
rationale_incorrect.C: Standard references describe comprehensive heart and lung evaluation procedures.
rationale_incorrect.D: Cardiopulmonary diagnostic evaluation is required beyond dental assessment alone.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: The evaluation process includes those procedures outlined in the sections above on heart and lung transplantation

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 1 → Heart/lung transplantation → 4. (evaluation includes heart and lung transplant procedures); PDF p. 39 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Fourth heart_lung organ tag in D2; evaluation-scope angle distinct from Eisenmenger indication (cctc-2013) and RHC monitoring (cctc-2057); anchor verified on Cupples p. 39.

stem: A candidate with short-bowel syndrome remains dependent on parenteral nutrition. Which finding supports the definition of intestinal failure used in transplant evaluation references?

options.text: Gut function is insufficient and intravenous supplementation is required to maintain health or growth
The patient eats a full oral diet without any nutritional support
Intestinal failure is defined only by cosmetic abdominal scarring
Intravenous supplementation is never part of intestinal failure definitions

explanation.rationale_correct: Intestinal failure is defined as gut function below the minimum needed for absorption of macronutrients and/or water and electrolytes such that intravenous supplementation is required to maintain health and/or growth.

rationale_incorrect.B: Intestinal failure implies insufficient gut function requiring intravenous supplementation rather than unrestricted oral intake alone.
rationale_incorrect.C: Intestinal failure is a functional nutritional definition, not a cosmetic diagnosis.
rationale_incorrect.D: Required intravenous supplementation is central to the definition of intestinal failure.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 13, Intestine Transplantation → Intestinal Failure → A.1.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: intravenous supplementation is required to maintain health and/or growth

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 13 → Intestinal Failure → A.1. (IV supplementation required to maintain health/growth); PDF p. 681 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Thirteenth 020300 item; intestinal-failure definition distinct from SOC suitability (cctc-2048) and late TPN discontinuation outcomes (cctc-3037); anchor verified on Cupples p. 681.

stem: When coordinating multidisciplinary consults for a pediatric solid-organ transplant candidate, which evaluation component aligns with standard references?

options.text: Psychosocial assessment including child development evaluation
Psychosocial assessment is omitted for all pediatric candidates
Only financial review without psychology or child development input
Child development evaluation replaces all medical testing

explanation.rationale_correct: Pediatric transplant psychosocial evaluation is completed by social work, psychology/psychiatry, and child development specialists and includes psychological status, coping, family support, adherence history, and related factors.

rationale_incorrect.B: Psychosocial and child development assessment is part of pediatric evaluation rather than being omitted.
rationale_incorrect.C: Child development and psychology input supplement rather than replace broader multidisciplinary assessment.
rationale_incorrect.D: Child development evaluation complements medical testing rather than replacing it.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 13, Pediatric Populations → psychosocial evaluation → vi.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Completed by social work, psychology/psychiatry, and child development (pediatrics)

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 13 → psychosocial evaluation → vi. (child development evaluation with social work and psychology/psychiatry); PDF p. 697 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Tenth 020200 item; ninth pediatric recipient in bank; child-development consult angle distinct from PCP coordination (cctc-2053); anchor verified on Cupples p. 697.
